title: AggregatedAssetsSnapshot
description: The one shared contract every connector emits into and the only shape core/ ever reads. See schema/README.md for narrative documentation of each field. This schema is bitemporal and content-addressed: every snapshot is immutable once written.

snapshot_id.description: Content hash of this snapshot's normalized payload (e.g. sha256 hex digest). Computed after normalization, before commit. Two snapshots with identical content must have identical snapshot_id — this is what makes 'no material change' detectable without comparing every field by hand.

observed_at.description: Wall-clock time this snapshot was assembled by the aggregation pipeline. Distinct from valid_from/valid_to, which describe the period the snapshot's data is asserted to represent.

valid_from.description: Start of the bitemporal validity window: the point from which this snapshot's facts are asserted true. TODO: define whether this can ever be backdated for a late-arriving connector run, and if so how commit_snapshot should treat ordering against an already-current snapshot with a later valid_from.

valid_to.description: End of the bitemporal validity window, or null while this snapshot is still current. Set only when a later snapshot supersedes this one — never mutated for any other reason, since snapshots are immutable.

scan_scope.description: Which scanners/tools actually ran and covered which assets in this snapshot. This is the mechanism that distinguishes 'this scanner didn't run against this asset' from 'this scanner ran and found nothing' — the latter is a real absence-of-finding, the former must never be read as one. TODO: finalize whether scope is expressed per-connector, per-asset, or as a cross product of the two; per-asset granularity is likely required once asset ownership is split across business units.

reachable_scanners.description: Scanner/connector identifiers that successfully ran and reported for (some or all of) this snapshot's asset population.

unreachable_scanners.description: Scanner/connector identifiers that were expected but did not run or could not be reached this cycle. A quality gate must reject any finding attributed to a scanner listed here.

coverage.description: Optional finer-grained record of which asset_ids each scanner actually covered, for organizations where scan scope varies per-asset rather than being all-or-nothing. TODO: decide if this is required once real deployments show scope is rarely uniform across the estate.

services.description: Business/technical services in scope, each carrying its own backup/DR posture. Services are the unit the FAIR engine attaches financial impact to (a service has a revenue-per-hour, a set of dependent assets, etc.) — TODO: confirm whether financial attributes belong here or purely in core/assumptions.py mapped by service criticality tier.

service_id.description: Stable identifier for this service, referenced by assets/endpoints that support it.

criticality.description: Business criticality tier. TODO: enumerate the fixed set of allowed values once the org's criticality taxonomy is settled — must never be an ordinal stuffed into a numeric field (see quality gate 5).

backup.description: Backup/DR posture for this service, used to derive RTO multipliers in core/assumptions.py.

last_tested_at.description: Null if never tested — must not be conflated with 'recently tested and fine'.

immutable_copy.description: Whether an offline/immutable backup copy exists (relevant to ransomware loss scenarios). TODO: confirm this is knowable from any connector or requires manual_attestation.

assets.description: Technical assets (hosts, workloads, identities-bearing systems, network devices) with their normalized findings and posture data from every connector that covers them.

asset_id.description: Resolved, stable identity for this asset across all connectors. Identity resolution (matching a Nessus host to a Prowler resource to a CMDB entry) happens in infra/connectors/ before this document is assembled — this field must never be a raw per-tool identifier.

service_ids.description: Which services (by service_id) this asset supports. An asset may support zero or more services.

findings.description: Normalized vulnerability/misconfiguration findings from any scanner (Nessus, Prowler, nmap, etc). Every finding must carry provenance (quality gate 4) and a criticality that is present or explicitly 'unknown' (quality gate 3) — never silently defaulted.

type.description: e.g. 'cve', 'misconfiguration', 'open_port'. TODO: enumerate once connector coverage is finalized.

epss_score.description: EPSS probability, [0,1], if this finding is CVE-backed. Populated by threat_intel_connector, not by the scanner connector itself.

kev_listed.description: Whether this CVE appears in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

criticality.description: Null is not the same as 'unknown' — use the literal string 'unknown' when a scanner reports a finding without a severity. Null means the field was never evaluated at all, which a quality gate should treat as a defect, not an absence.

provenance.description: Which connector and raw source produced this finding — mandatory, never null (quality gate 4).

raw_source_id.description: The tool-native identifier this was normalized from, kept for auditability/debugging only — must never be read by core/ or governance/.

remediated_at.description: Null while open. Distinguishing 'remediated' from 'scanner stopped reporting it because the scanner went dark' is exactly what scan_scope is for — this field alone is not sufficient evidence of remediation if the relevant scanner is in unreachable_scanners.

counts_toward_loss.description: Optional; absent means true. false marks a finding as corroborating evidence only: it stays in the snapshot (visible, and usable as compliance evidence) but is NOT turned into a separate loss-event scenario by the engine. Use it when a source overlaps another scanner's coverage, so the same underlying issue is not counted twice. It is not a remediation claim and must never be used to hide a finding.

threat_intel.description: Threat-intelligence context attached to this asset (beyond per-finding EPSS/KEV), e.g. active campaigns targeting this asset's exposed services. TODO: define shape once threat_intel_connector's real data sources are chosen.

edr.description: EDR/endpoint posture and alert summary for this asset from wazuh_connector or equivalent.

detection_rules_active.description: TODO: confirm whether the engine needs rule-level granularity to model control overlap (principle 7) or a coarser coverage summary suffices.

recent_alerts.description: TODO: define alert shape once wazuh_connector's normalization is designed.

identity_access.description: IAM posture relevant to this asset from iam_connector, e.g. privileged accounts with access, MFA coverage.

network.description: Network exposure posture for this asset from nmap_connector, e.g. internet-facing status and open ports.

segment_id.description: Which network_topology.segments entry this asset belongs to, for attack-graph edge derivation. Null means segment membership is unknown — core/ must treat this as maximum uncertainty (could be anywhere, potentially adjacent to anything), never as 'isolated' or 'no path in or out'. Optional and independent of scan_scope: a connector can resolve segment_id without running a full network scan.

network_topology.description: Network segmentation used to derive attack-graph edges between assets (see core/engine/attack_graph.py). Optional at the top level — a snapshot with no network_topology has no known segmentation, and every asset's reachability must be treated as unknown rather than as 'unreachable'. Assets sharing the same non-null segment_id are considered mutually reachable; reachability *between* different segments exists only where segment_reachability explicitly lists it — nothing is inferred.

segments.description: Every known network segment/zone, referenced by assets[].network.segment_id.

segment_reachability.description: Directed edges between segments. A listed {from_segment_id, to_segment_id} pair means an attacker already inside from_segment_id can reach to_segment_id (e.g. a firewall rule permits it) — this is directional and not automatically symmetric. Absence of a pair means no assumed reachability; this must be populated explicitly by a connector with real topology visibility, never guessed at by core/.

endpoints.description: Network-addressable endpoints (IPs/hostnames/URLs) discovered by cmdb_connector/nmap_connector, prior to or independent of asset_id resolution. TODO: clarify the exact relationship between an 'endpoint' and an 'asset' — whether every endpoint must eventually resolve to exactly one asset_id, or whether unresolved endpoints are a valid (flagged) terminal state.

resolved_asset_id.description: Null if this endpoint has not yet been resolved to a known asset_id.
